ruling.recommended_action: Uphold the $6.61 rider cancellation fee; no refund, no account flag — advise the rider (if she appeals) that her remedy is a discretionary RydeHELP voucher request under NS-7.
ruling.reasoning:
The trace settles the governing branch: this is a rider cancellation of an instant RydeX booking [F4], so NS-0 routes the fee question to NS-4, not to the no-show branch. The rider cancelled at 08:46:40, 6 min 40 s (400 s) after acceptance at 08:40:00 [F4], i.e. beyond the 3-minute free-cancellation window, so the $6.61 fee is chargeable [F4][F7][NS-0][NS-4]. No refund item arises: the fee is the published $6.61 with surge 1.0× and nothing unpublished added [F7][F8][FARE-1].

The rider's fairness complaint — "the driver had not even arrived" — is contradicted by the GPS and timeline records, which take precedence over statements. The driver was first within 200 m of the pickup at 08:41:25, accumulated 5 min 15 s within 200 m before the cancellation, and was closest at 39 m at 08:46:10 [F1][F2][F5]. He tapped "I'm Here" at 08:42:15 while 40 m from the pickup and stayed within 200 m for 4 min 25 s after the tap [F6], stationary 41 m from the pickup from 08:42:00 to the cancellation [F3]. So even on the driver-side NS-1 conditions (arrival tap at the pickup, presence within 200 m at the tap, continued waiting past the 3-minute mark) the record supports the fee [F3][F6][NS-1]; and it removes any driver-fault ground for a waiver.

The rider's own message, "Sorry, plans changed, I will cancel" at 08:45 [F10], is a voluntary cancellation unrelated to driver conduct; the driver's arrival message [F9] and the rider's message are both timestamped in a complete 2-message chat record [F11], so the timing is reliable and no G12 incompleteness arises. No traffic incident or congestion band existed on the route and the weather was fair [F13][F14][F15], so no RD-4 reasonable-cause branch is engaged [RD-4]. The rider does not contest the fee on its merits, and the advocates converge on no_action; the fee is timely disputed within the 30-day window [F4][F7][NS-7].

Profile facts do not decide anything here: the rider's clean 90-day record [F16] gives no ground to waive a charge valid under NS-4, and the driver's history [F17] is not a repeated-violation pattern, so no flag_account arises under RD-6 [F16][F17][RD-6].

Safety screen: I read the two chat messages [F9][F10], the driver's statement [F12] and the complaint. They contain only an arrival notice, a courtesy cancellation message and a factual account of parking at the pickup; there is no threat, intimidation, harassment, sexual remark or dangerous-driving allegation, so safety_concern = none [F9][F10][F12][SAFE-1]. Evidence is sufficient: every element the ruling needs (who cancelled, when, fare amount, driver's position and waiting) is settled by the system record [F4][F1][F2][F3][F6][F7].

rejected_claims.reason: The rider's claim that the driver had not arrived (and thus the fee is unfair) is contradicted by the system record: the driver was first within 200 m at 08:41:25 and closest at 39 m at 08:46:10 [F1][F2], and Ryde publishes no ETA-delay waiver, so no ground to reduce or waive the fee under NS-4 exists — the fee stands [F4][F7][NS-4].

The rider's residual reliance on FARE-1 yields nothing: the $6.61 charged is the published cancellation fee with no surge [F7][F8] and no unpublished add-on appears, so FARE-1 produces no refund item [F7][F8][FARE-1].

The driver's NS-1(i)-(iii) showing is not the governing branch: the cancellation was by the rider, so NS-0/NS-4 decides and the NS-1 arrival and waiting conditions are supporting evidence only, not the basis of the fee [F4][NS-0][NS-4][NS-1].

The driver's statement that he was parked at the pickup [F12] adds nothing beyond the GPS, which already shows him stationary 41 m from the pickup from 08:42:00 to 08:46:40 [F3]; the statement is corroborated but is not needed for, and does not decide, the outcome under NS-4 [F3][F12][NS-4].

The absence of traffic and congestion records [F13][F14] and the fair weather [F15] engage nothing: there is no off-route segment and no RD-4 reasonable-cause branch in this rider-cancellation case, so RD-4 has nothing to excuse [F13][F14][F15][RD-4].
